question: If sqrt{x} = 11, what is the value of x + sqrt{x}?
solution:
Here is the HTML output based on the given question: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If √x = 11, then x = 11² = 121.

Now, x + √x = 121 + 11.

∴ Answer = 132

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√x = 11

**Formula used:**

x + √x = x + square root of x

 x = 121 √x = 11 
• x + √x 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = 11² = 121

⇒ x + √x = 121 + 11 = 132

**∴ The correct answer is 132.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root Basics

The square root of a number y is the value which, when squared, gives y. Example: √121 = 11.

Perfect Squares

A perfect square is a number that has an integer as its square root. Example: 121 is a perfect square of 11.

Addition with Square Roots

When adding a square root and its square, compute each separately and then sum. Example: x + √x.
